title: Preflight: Abort criteria, rapid rollback choreography, and incident comms templates for runtime-1.22
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Create a concise, operational preflight artifact that defines concrete abort criteria, the step-by-step choreography for a fast rollback, and ready-to-send incident and rollback communications for the runtime-1.22 launch. Goal is to reduce decision latency during a launch problem and ensure consistent messaging across Eng, Support, Sales, and Customer Success. This ticket owns the PM deliverable and coordiantes reviews from Eng, SRE, Legal, and GTM.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A single-page abort criteria table (metric -> threshold -> owner -> action) is approved by SRE and ENG leads
A2: Rollback choreography doc (play-by-play for 0–30 minutes, 30–120 minutes, and postmortem) reviewed by ENG, Infra, and Ops
A3: Incident and rollback comms templates reviewed and signed off by Support, Legal, and Comms
A4: A lightweight runbook checklist is loaded into the launch channel and applied during the staged canary rollout
A5: Dry run performed in the 2026-W12 staging window with timeline <45 minutes for simulated rollback execution
prelaunch_checks: Verify canary routing is enabled and traffic split can be adjusted via Console
Confirm monitoring alerts (latency P95, error-rate, token-queue-depth) are wired to PagerDuty and the launch channel
Ensure fallback model variants are available in the same region and that KMS keys are accessible
Confirm on-call SRE and runtime engineers are scheduled for the launch window
Validate that dedicated capacity auto-burst limits and quotas are known and documented
abort_criteria: Sustained >3x baseline P95 latency for 10m despite autoscaling and cache warmup -> abort
Error rate >2% of requests for 5m with correlated 5xx increase and no immediate fix -> abort
Data-sensitivity or privacy violation detected in outputs or logs -> immediate abort and legal notified
KV-cache corruption or persistent deserialization errors in >1 node cluster -> abort
Unrecoverable model quality degradation (regression flagged by eval harness affecting >=5% of core prompts) -> abort
rollback_plan_summary: Fast rollback will be a three-phase choreography: (1) Immediate mitigation (0–10m): stop canary traffic, route new traffic to last-known-good model variant, enable verbose tracing; (2) Stabilization (10–60m): run smoke tests, validate metrics across regions, rollback any infra knobs; (3) Recovery & follow-up (60–180m): execute full rollback for all traffic if stabilization fails, trigger postmortem, and prepare customer comms. Primary rollback mechanism: Console routing rollback to runtime-1.21 instance group or fallback quantized variant. Secondary mechanism: Throttle ingress at edge and revert to cached responses for rate-limited tiers.
comms_templates: Incident - Initial (to internal channel): [INCIDENT] runtime-1.22 canary - elevated P95 latency. Time: {{time}}. Observed: P95 x3 baseline, error-rate increased from 0.2% to 2.1%. Action: canary traffic paused, fallback routing enabled. Owners: @miguel.santos (Runtime), @sre-oncall. Next update in 15 minutes.

Incident - Customer-facing (to affected customers): Subject: Temporary degradation observed for API latency. Body: We detected increased latency for a small portion of API requests during a staged update. We have paused the rollout and routed affected traffic to a known-good version while we investigate. There should be no data loss. We'll provide updates within 30 minutes. Contact: support@redwood.com.

Rollback Announcement (internal): Rolling back runtime-1.22 to runtime-1.21 due to sustained P95 regression in canary. Start: {{time}}. Steps executed: canary paused, traffic redirected, smoke suite run. Expected completion: +15 minutes. Postmortem owners: @miguel.santos, @riley.chen, @ops-lead.

Rollback Announcement (public status page): A rollback is in progress for a recent runtime deployment due to performance regressions. We are reverting to the previous version to restore normal service; intermittent errors or higher latency may persist during the rollback window. Status updates posted to status.redwood.com.

Postmortem invite template: We will run a 60-minute investigation meeting at {{time+2h}} with Eng, SRE, Product, and CS. Required pre-reads: canary metrics snapshot, error traces, and deploy diff. Expected deliverable: blameless postmortem and action items.

Customer success outreach template: Hi {{customer_name}}, during a staged runtime update we observed degraded performance for a subset of requests affecting your org. We routed traffic back to the prior version and are investigating. We expect a full remediation timeline within 24 hours. A senior Eng will reach out if you have a prioritized SLA incident.

External press/legal hold template: [CONFIDENTIAL] We are executing an internal rollback of a runtime deployment. Legal and Comms have been notified. Do not disclose details externally until internal briefing completed.
